Just browsing through here for a few hours and I've noticed a few stories displayed multiple times because they've been submitted to more than one subverse.

I can understand the difficulty in deciding sometimes whether a story should be linked to /News or /Technology or /Science, for example.

I've also noticed over the years of using other sites that when multiple people in different threads (same topic) say the same thing, there is an urge to reply with the same text multiple times.

Perhaps there should be a system for allowing subverse-ambiguous posts to be posted to multiple subverses, with a limit of up to 3? Also, if someone has posted the same topic to multiple subverses, can the link on the front page automatically display the various subverse links instead of showing the multiple submissions?

With regards to commenting, it would be nice if there was a way to tag multiple comments (up to 5?) that say the same thing and then reply to all with one message - with a designator showing that replica comments in a thread are not the author repeating themselves but simply replying to more than one person.

With regards to commenting...

I like this idea, but I'm trying to imagine how the layout would look. Is there any way to display such branching-and-merging conversations without replicating comments exponentially (1, 5, 25, 125...) as the discussion progresses?

I personally view it as the one comment being replied to all of the other comments and subsequently linked into one (so, if you were to permalink one of the "replies", you'd get the same permalink for the other replies), and the discussion being continued on that one comment.

It could be something as simple as the first of several duplicate replies looks normal while subsequent replies are shortened to one line ending in ... and the rest of the comment is hidden or greyed out.

There's no real change made to the flow of the comments and anyone who sees a greyed duplicate reply can perhaps click on the ... to expand the comment or skip over it, knowing they've already read it.

What do you think about having a small portion of the /user/name page customizable by the user?

Maybe this recalls unwelcome memories of old-style social networking sites (like Facebook etc.) where the focus is more about who you are than what you say. I like the "stupid is as stupid does" mindset engendered by the downplaying of users' identities.

On the other hand, it'd be nice to be able to list a few things about myself, such as my accounts on (ahem) other websites. That might aid in establishing a new community here. Also, it could be useful if I could list my bitcoin/dogecoin addresses, so that people could tip me without there needing to be a bot for it. (Though admittedly, not many people will care about that.)

Sounds like myspace, but hell, why not. Some people would like to reveal more information about their hobbies etc and perhaps customize their profile in a way so this is certainly going to be considered if enough people request it.
I think it's a cool idea, maybe have a spot for pic links from imgur (or whoaverse alternative).
Yes, something like an editable sidebar for users would be useful.

I am in favor of this idea.

An important thing to note is that there are both users who would go for and utilize this feature set (which I feel would be beneficial in expanding the social aspect of the site), and those that are primarily interested only in semi-anonymous postings with little interest in things of this sort.

Over at /r/zenonnet, we had a discussion on this where opinion was roughly split 50/50. Half of the users were against the idea because they did not like the whole karma-accumulation aspect and wanted to ramp down on that too. These are the people who stress that the appeal of a site like reddit is that it is unlike FB or Myspace in that little real world identity information is shown.

However, I feel a compromise can be made that would cater to both parties. Very simply put, allow any customization to be completely optional. If anyone uses Skype, you'll note that that they give you the ability to "hide" most of the "stats" on your profile. We could use such a thing where even users who don't like the idea of karma or imaginary internet points could hide their karma on their userpage and any of the newer profile customization variables could also be hidden or not filled in.
I second (or third where in line I am) this idea, and agree that the ability to hide those additional information categories would serve both sides.
